settings.headline: Numbing cream for semi-permanent makeup, matched to the sitting.
settings.subhead: Microblading, lip blush and brow work are precise, close work on some of the most sensitive skin on the face — small areas, but exacting ones, often over a long sitting. Gel suits it well: it goes exactly where the artist needs it and holds through the sitting. Cream works too. Advanced is the strength most sittings call for. Here's how to choose.
settings.image_alt: Senseless Clinical Strength Comfort Cream and Comfort Gel — semi-permanent makeup

settings.headline: Small area, long sitting
settings.body: SPMU is slow, close work, and the skin feels every pass — brows, lash line and lips are sensitive by nature, and a sitting can run well over an hour without a pause. The area is small, so a precise format that stays exactly where it's placed suits it, and the length of the sitting is why many book beyond the entry strength. Match the prep to the sitting you're actually booked for.

settings.matched: Shorter, routine appointments, smaller areas, and anyone starting out who wants to begin considered.
Longer or more sensitive sessions and larger areas — the one most people settle on for regular aesthetic work.

settings.headline: Match your numbing cream for SPMU to the sitting
settings.body: None of the three is "better" than another — each is formulated for a different kind of sitting. For SPMU, most people start at Advanced.
settings.note: If you're between two, the lower one is usually the sensible start, and you can move up next time.

settings.caption: Precise facial format, the usual SPMU pick.

settings.heading: Gel or cream for SPMU?
settings.body: Gel applies exactly to a small area — brows, lash line, lips — and holds through a long sitting. Cream works the same way if you prefer its feel. Same strengths across every format — choose by preference or your artist's protocol.

settings.heading: Before you buy: the bit most sellers skip
settings.body: Many SPMU artists apply their own numbing as part of the sitting, and some have a specific product or routine they prefer you not to interfere with. If yours does, you may not need to bring your own — and turning up already prepared without asking can affect how the pigment takes. Self-applied prep matters most where the artist doesn't provide it, or where they're happy for you to prepare beforehand. A quick message before you book settles it.

settings.question: Which strength should I use for microblading?
settings.answer: Most people use Advanced — microblading is sustained work on sensitive skin. Clinical suits shorter touch-ups; Professional the longest sittings or particularly sensitive skin. If you're between two, start with the lower one.

settings.question: Which strength for lip blush?
settings.answer: Same approach — Advanced as the standard choice, Professional for longer sittings. Lips are sensitive and lip blush runs long, so it often asks a little more of the prep than a brow sitting.

settings.question: Does microblading hurt?
settings.answer: Most people describe it as scratching rather than sharp, and numbing is a cosmetic preparation that supports comfort, not an anaesthetic. How it feels varies with the area, the technique and your own sensitivity. Your artist can tell you what to expect for your sitting.

settings.question: Does lip blush hurt?
settings.answer: Lips are more sensitive than brows, so it tends to be felt more. Your artist will guide the prep that suits the sitting.

settings.question: Gel or cream for SPMU?
settings.answer: Either. Gel is the usual pick — precise on a small area and it holds through a long sitting; cream is the equal alternative. Spray isn't suitable here. Same strengths across both.

settings.question: Do I need to patch test?
settings.answer: Yes — patch test 24 hours before on the inside of your wrist or behind your ear, and don't use it if you see any reaction. Take extra care around the eyes and lips, and on sensitive skin.

settings.heading: Not sure which to choose?
settings.body: Answer three quick questions — treatment, skin and session length — and we'll point you to the format and strength we'd reach for.
